items.evidence: Notes do not mention the project manager opening the meeting or stating the agenda.

"75% find remotes ugly", "80% willing pay more for style", "Younger prefer voice recognition", "Over 50% frustrated losing remotes", "Users use 10% buttons", "Channel, volume most used", "Less is more design principle".
Section "User Interface Design" covers "Aim for conventional layout", "Room for novel design", but not the description of what a remote is or the design approach (specs, prototypes, feedback).
"Fully featured vs basic remotes" and "Balance simple vs advanced" mention the two remotes but not their specific advantages and disadvantages.
"Infrared preferred communication", "Chip converts energy to data", "Four parts: battery, chip, user, infrared bulb".
"New Requirements & Target Market" section plus target group, "Voice recognition rejected (price)", "Prevent remote loss feature", "Battery options considered".
No mention of the questionnaire and summary.
No mention of individual work time.
No mention of the project manager posting minutes and documentation.
No mention of team members posting their documentation.
No mention of the industrial designer's components concept.
No mention of the user interface concept task.
No mention of trend watching for the marketing expert.
"No Teletext support".
"Focus only TV remote".
"Use corporate yellow/black colors" covers colour but not the slogan or the general requirement that the corporate image be recognisable.
"Emphasize simplicity and fashion".
Notes say "Target group 15-35 years"; transcript shows the team concluded it was more useful to define objectives like fashion and simplicity than a specific age group.
"Prevent remote loss feature".
"Large buttons for essentials".
"Hidden advanced functions" conveys the extra functions are available.
"Hidden advanced functions".
"Rechargeable via cradle possible" under "Battery options considered" frames it as an option, not a decision (PM: "that's a good idea, we'll keep it").
Target group is discussed but presented as settled ("Target group 15-35 years") rather than as an unresolved difficulty.
"Voice recognition rejected (price)".
Only "Reliable infrared signal" as a design priority; the discussion of how to make infra-red more functional (battery, chip quality) is absent.
"Battery options considered", "Rechargeable via cradle possible", "Minimize battery changes".

errors.why_wrong: 15-35 was only the voice-recognition age split; the team found it hard to narrow, mentioned under 65 and other ranges, and decided to define objectives (fashion, simplicity) instead of an age group.

errors.claim: Investigate technical feasibility for rechargeable battery
errors.why_wrong: Nobody agreed to this task; the user interface designer only suggested investigating whether a battery is needed at all, and the charging station was discussed as an idea.
